thesis: World's largest gold producer and the only gold miner in the S&P 500, guiding 5.26 million attributable ounces in 2026 at by-product AISC of $1,680/oz from a 13-mine core portfolio plus the 38.5% Nevada Gold Mines JV. H1 2026 delivered sales of $13.4B (+30% YoY), net income of $5.46B and record free cash flow of $5.35B at a $4,661/oz realized gold price, funding a $1.04 annualized dividend and $3.5B of buybacks that have cut the share count roughly 9% since February 2024. At $116.05 the stock trades on ~12.8x FY2026 consensus EPS of ~$9.09 and ~7x trailing adjusted EBITDA of $16.8B with a net cash balance sheet. The stock has de-rated with bullion, which sits ~26% below its January 2026 peak of ~$5,608/oz as the Fed resumed hiking — gold price direction remains the dominant variable.

financials.gross_margin: ~70% (sales less costs applicable to sales, H1 2026)

drivers: Gold recovers toward $5,000–$5,500/oz as central bank buying and policy uncertainty reassert themselves; every $100/oz adds ~$505M of pre-tax revenue
2026 guidance met at 5.26Moz with by-product AISC tracking below the $1,680/oz plan (YTD $1,321/oz)
Buyback continues at pace — $4.3B remains of the $6B authorization — compounding per-share FCF and dividend growth
Red Chris Block Cave reaches a positive final investment decision and Cadia PC1-2, Tanami Expansion 2 and Cerro Negro Expansion add long-life ounces
Nevada Gold Mines JV settlement creates a ~100Moz Nevada complex, unlocking Fourmile, Mike and Fiberline value

base_case.assumptions: Gold averages $4,200–$4,600/oz through 2027, in line with the $4,500/oz guidance assumption. FY2026 attributable production lands near 5.26Moz with by-product AISC of $1,500–$1,680/oz. FY2026 EPS approximates the ~$9.09 consensus and free cash flow of roughly $8.5–9.0B (estimate, not company-guided) funds the $1.1B dividend plus ongoing repurchases. Multiple stays in a 13–15x earnings band.

risks: Gold retraces to $3,500–$3,800/oz on further Fed tightening and 5%+ long-end Treasury yields, compressing margins and the multiple together
Cost inflation from higher Ghanaian royalties, diesel and labour pushes AISC above guidance
Repeat geotechnical or seismic disruption at Cadia, Lihir or Brucejack cuts production and lifts unit costs
Jurisdictional or FX shocks across PNG, Peru, Argentina, Ghana, Suriname and Mexico
Reclamation drag persists: $6.2B of reclamation liabilities with ~$1.8B of Yanacocha water treatment spend ($1.1B incurred) before normalising in 2028

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 results — production broadly flat sequentially, with higher sustaining and development capital and the $1.95B Barrick payment hitting cash flow
Red Chris Block Cave final investment decision following British Columbia environmental and Mines Act approvals
FY2026 results, 2027 production and cost guidance, and the annual per-share dividend reset off a lower share count
Share repurchases under the $6B authorization — $4.3B remaining as of the Q2 filing
Gold price path and Federal Reserve policy — bullion near $4,150/oz versus the $4,500/oz guidance assumption

key_risks: Gold price volatility — bullion is ~26% below its January 2026 peak of ~$5,608/oz and the equity is a levered proxy
Rate and real-yield risk: the Fed hiked in September 2026 and the 30-year Treasury yield reached 5.53%, its highest since 2004
Unit cost inflation — Q2 by-product AISC jumped to $1,621/oz on Ghana royalties, diesel and Cadia downtime costs
Operational and geotechnical risk at large block-cave and refractory assets (Cadia seismic event in April 2026, Lihir, Brucejack)
Geopolitical and FX exposure across PNG, Peru, Argentina, Ghana, Suriname and Mexico
$6.2B reclamation and remediation liabilities, including the ~$1.8B Yanacocha water treatment programme
Capital allocation: the $1.95B cash payment to Barrick reduces the net cash buffer that underpins the through-cycle dividend
